title: Vans for a food bank's weekend drive

blocks.text: A food bank (not GridCap) leases vans for its weekend drive. Each van type $`t`$ carries $`\text{cap}_t`$ pallets and costs $`c_t`$ dollars for the weekend. The dealer has $`a_t`$ vans of the type, and leases them only in packs of $`k_t`$ (a pack of 2 means 0, 2, 4, ... vans). The drive must move `demand` pallets, the board approved `budget` dollars, and every van needs one of the `drivers` volunteers.
Write `build(types, demand, budget, drivers)` in `vans.py`. It returns a CP-SAT model and a dict `n` of its variables, one per van type, keyed by the type's name. The model is:

\begin{aligned}
\min \;& \sum_{t \in T} c_t\, n_t \\
\text{s.t. }& \sum_{t \in T} \text{cap}_t\, n_t \ge \text{demand} && \text{(cover)} \\
& \sum_{t \in T} c_t\, n_t \le \text{budget} && \text{(budget)} \\
& \sum_{t \in T} n_t \le \text{drivers} && \text{(drivers)} \\
& n_t \in \{0, k_t, 2k_t, \dots\},\ n_t \le a_t && \forall t \in T
\end{aligned}
The last line is each variable's domain, not a row: give every $`n_t`$ exactly the values a lease allows when you create it.
The tests fix every $`n_t`$ to a value with an equality and ask CP-SAT whether the model still has a solution, so they check which fleets your model allows and refuses. About eight lines.

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from ortools.sat.python import cp_model


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class VanType:
    name: str
    capacity: int     # pallets per van
    cost: int         # dollars for the weekend
    available: int    # vans of this type the dealer has
    pack: int         # vans of this type are leased in packs of this many


def build(types: list[VanType], demand: int, budget: int, drivers: int) -> tuple[cp_model.CpModel, dict]:
    """The cheapest fleet that carries the demand, within the budget and the drivers."""
    model = cp_model.CpModel()
    n = {}
    for t in types:
        packs = cp_model.Domain.from_values(range(0, t.available + 1, t.pack))
        n[t.name] = model.new_int_var_from_domain(packs, f"n_{t.name}")
    model.add(sum(t.capacity * n[t.name] for t in types) >= demand)
    model.add(sum(t.cost * n[t.name] for t in types) <= budget)
    model.add(sum(n.values()) <= drivers)
    model.minimize(sum(t.cost * n[t.name] for t in types))
    return model, n


if __name__ == "__main__":
    fleet = [VanType("small", 4, 300, 6, 2), VanType("box", 10, 650, 3, 1)]
    model, n = build(fleet, 30, 3_000, 5)
    solver = cp_model.CpSolver()
    status = solver.solve(model)
    print(solver.status_name(status), {name: solver.value(v) for name, v in n.items()})

import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from ortools.sat.python import cp_model

from vans import VanType, build

fleet = [VanType("cargo", 6, 400, 4, 2), VanType("truck", 15, 900, 2, 1), VanType("mini", 3, 150, 6, 3)]

for demand, budget, drivers in ((30, 3_000, 5), (45, 2_500, 4)):
    model, n = build(fleet, demand, budget, drivers)
    solver = cp_model.CpSolver()
    solver.parameters.max_time_in_seconds = 10
    status = solver.solve(model)
    label = f"demand {demand}, budget {budget}, drivers {drivers}:"
    if status in (cp_model.OPTIMAL, cp_model.FEASIBLE):
        print(label, solver.status_name(status), {name: solver.value(v) for name, v in n.items()},
              "cost", round(solver.objective_value))
    else:
        print(label, solver.status_name(status))

cases.says: a fleet that carries the demand is allowed, and one a few pallets short is refused
a fleet within the budget is allowed, and a dearer one is refused
a fleet with one van per driver is allowed, and one with more vans than drivers is refused
a count that is not a whole number of packs is refused even when every row holds
a count above what the dealer has is refused even when it is a whole number of packs

origin.section: A Linear Constraint Has Whole-Number Coefficients

concepts: every CP-SAT variable is an integer with a finite domain, given as bounds or as a listed set of values
linear constraints take whole-number coefficients and bounds, and ranges and not-equal are allowed
